questions.stem: The Indian National Congress was founded in 1885 by:

options.option_text: Allan Octavian Hume (with W.C. Bonnerjee, Dadabhai Naoroji and others)

questions.explanation: INC — founded 28 December 1885 at Gokuldas Tejpal Sanskrit College, Bombay. Founder — A.O. Hume (retired ICS officer, ornithologist). 72 delegates attended the first session. First President — Womesh Chandra Bonnerjee (W.C. Bonnerjee). Lord Dufferin was the supportive Viceroy. Original goals — increase Indian representation, civil service exams to be held in India, less budget on military. Hume is often called 'Father of INC'. The INC moved through phases: Moderates (1885-1905), Extremists (1905-1919), Gandhian (1919-1947).

questions.stem: The first WOMAN President of the Indian National Congress was:
questions.explanation: Annie Besant — Irish-born theosophist, women's rights activist, Home Rule League founder (1916). Presided over the 1917 Calcutta session of INC — first woman president. Sarojini Naidu — first INDIAN woman president, 1925 Kanpur session. Indira Gandhi — president 1959. Sonia Gandhi — longest-serving president (1998-2017). Nellie Sengupta — second Indian woman president (1933 Calcutta, in absentia). Other notable presidents: W.C. Bonnerjee (1885), Dadabhai Naoroji (1886, 1893, 1906), G.K. Gokhale (1905).

questions.stem: The famous 'Purna Swaraj' (Complete Independence) resolution was passed at which INC session?
questions.explanation: LAHORE Session, December 1929 (29-31). Presided by Jawaharlal Nehru (youngest INC President). Adopted 'Purna Swaraj' (Complete Independence) as the goal — replacing earlier 'Dominion Status' demand. 26 January 1930 declared as Independence Day (later moved as REPUBLIC DAY when constitution came into force in 1950). Tricolour hoisted on banks of Ravi. Decision led to the Civil Disobedience Movement starting March 1930 (Dandi March 12 March-6 April).

questions.stem: The 'Lucknow Pact' between INC and Muslim League — agreeing on separate electorates and joint demand for self-rule — was signed at the 1916 INC session presided by:
questions.explanation: Lucknow Pact — December 1916. INC session presided by AMBIKA CHARAN MAZUMDAR. Reunited INC's Moderate (Mehta) and Extremist (Tilak) factions after 1907 Surat split. Simultaneously, Muslim League (held its session same time, same city) signed pact with INC accepting separate electorates for Muslims in exchange for joint demand of self-government. Architects — Tilak + Jinnah (then in INC + ML). Lucknow Pact also marked Jinnah's high water-mark of 'ambassador of Hindu-Muslim unity' (Sarojini Naidu's phrase).

questions.stem: Subhas Chandra Bose presided over which INC session, after which he resigned due to differences with Gandhi?

options.option_text: Tripuri 1939 (his 2nd presidency, defeating Gandhi's nominee Pattabhi Sitaramayya)

questions.explanation: Bose presided 1938 (Haripura, supported by Gandhi) and 1939 (Tripuri, defeating Pattabhi Sitaramayya — Gandhi's choice — by 1,580 vs 1,377 votes). Differences widened — Bose wanted aggressive 6-month ultimatum to British. Working Committee (Gandhi loyalists) refused to cooperate. Bose resigned Tripuri presidency in April 1939, founded the Forward Bloc within INC. Later left India 1941 — Berlin → Tokyo → Singapore — INA leadership in 1943. Famous 'Chalo Delhi' + 'You give me blood, I will give you freedom'.

options.option_text: Split between Moderates (led by G.K. Gokhale) and Extremists (led by B.G. Tilak)
First-ever INC president from South India

questions.explanation: Surat Split — 1907 INC session at Surat (Gujarat). Issues: which programme to adopt — Moderates wanted to consolidate the partition-of-Bengal era methods (petitions, prayers, protests), while Extremists (Tilak, Lal-Bal-Pal) demanded swadeshi + boycott + national education + passive resistance. Physical altercation at Surat over the choice of presidential candidate led to a permanent split. Re-united at Lucknow 1916. Pre-Surat both sides had functioned within INC; after, parallel programmes.

questions.stem: Mahatma Gandhi presided over the INC only ONCE. The session was at:
questions.explanation: Gandhi was INC President only once — at Belgaum, Karnataka, December 1924. He focused on Hindu-Muslim unity, removal of untouchability, khadi promotion. Rest of the time he led the movement WITHOUT formal INC office — exercising informal moral authority. Other notable single-time presidents: Subhas Bose (1938, 1939). Multiple-time presidents: Dadabhai Naoroji (3 times), Surendranath Banerjee (2), Sonia Gandhi (longest non-stop tenure 1998-2017). Last pre-independence president — J.B. Kripalani 1947.
